     Cherries are delightful stone fruits celebrated for their
     deep crimson colors and distinctly sweet or tart flavors
     depending on the variety selected. These small, jewel-like
     fruits are rich in antioxidants and vitamin C, supporting
     immune function and overall health throughout the year.
     Cherries have a short summer season when they're at their
     peak, though they can be dried, frozen, or preserved for
     year-round enjoyment. Whether enjoyed fresh by the handful,
     added to fruit salads, or baked into elegant pies,
     cherries bring natural sweetness and visual appeal. Their
     sophisticated taste makes them favorites for both casual
     snacking and fine desserts.
  4. Date
     Dates are ancient fruits cultivated in warm climates for
     thousands of years, holding special significance in Middle
     Eastern and North African cuisine and culture. These
     caramel-colored fruits are naturally sweet with a chewy
     texture, packed with fiber, potassium, and natural sugars
     that provide quick energy. Dates work wonderfully as
     standalone snacks, stuffed with almonds or cheese, or
     blended into nutritious energy balls and smoothies. Their
     natural sweetness makes them excellent replacements for
     refined sugar in baking and cooking. With varieties like
     Medjool and Deglet Noor offering distinct characteristics,
     dates bring versatility and tradition to any kitchen.
